claims.text: Low-temperature ID-HVAF deposition with a propylene-fueled i7 torch will improve the durability and reliability of FeCoNiCrAl bond coats.
The proposed deposition process preserves a refined FeCoNiCrAl microstructure.
The proposed deposition process produces fewer unwanted oxide phases during deposition.
Traditional high-temperature deposition of FeCoNiCrAl bond coats tends to cause significant oxidation.
Traditional high-temperature deposition of FeCoNiCrAl bond coats tends to produce microstructural defects.
The intervention will produce a finer and more homogeneous bond-coat microstructure.
The intervention will reduce oxide-phase formation at the bond-coat/substrate interface.
Lower deposition temperatures reduce premature oxidation during deposition.
Lower deposition temperatures reduce microstructural degradation during deposition.
Reduced oxidation and microstructural degradation lead to a denser coating.
Reduced oxidation and microstructural degradation lead to a better-adhered coating.
A denser, better-adhered coating withstands service-related mechanical and thermal stresses more effectively.
ID-HVAF-deposited bond coats will have greater adhesion than conventionally deposited controls after thermal cycling.
ID-HVAF-deposited bond coats will have lower spallation rates than conventionally deposited controls after thermal cycling.
ID-HVAF-deposited bond coats will have greater overall durability under thermal cycling than conventionally deposited controls.
The benefits of the intervention should persist under high-temperature operation and repeated thermal cycling.
The improvement may be limited if low-temperature deposition does not sufficiently activate interfacial bonding mechanisms.
The improvement may be lost when operating temperatures exceed the tolerance of the refined microstructure.
Process inconsistencies introduced during scale-up may diminish the durability benefit.
